name: Alex The Handyman
language_note: No Spanish-language content found anywhere for this business (Google Maps listing is English-only, no social profiles, no reviews text captured beyond the brief's theme tags). Pembroke Pines is a mixed English/Spanish market, but with no direct evidence either way, default language set to English per pipeline rule.
dm_message: Hi! I came across Alex The Handyman, a perfect 5.0 rating with 14 reviews on Google, reviewers keep calling the work honest and reliable. Noticed there is no website yet, so I built a free sample one: https://siteforge-demos.odd-forest-9504.workers.dev/alexthehandymanpembrokepines/ Nothing changes on your end. Like it? We move it to your own domain. Not for you? We take it down, no obligation. Michael Vargas / Merktop

owner.note: The Google Business Profile photos are credited to uploader 'alex plishtiev', which strongly suggests the owner's name is Alex Plishtiev (matches the business name 'Alex The Handyman'). This is a plausible but not independently confirmed match (no second source), so the last name was NOT used anywhere on the site or in outreach copy; only 'Alex' is used, which is already the business's own name.

phone_source: Live Google Maps listing fetch (scripts/gmaps_detail.js, Playwright), confirmed 2026-08-14: 'Phone: +1 917-306-7075'. Area code 917 is New York City; the Maps listing itself is physically pinned in Pembroke Pines, FL (lat 25.782414, lon -80.2253934), consistent with a mobile number kept from a prior NY location, not a sign the business is not FL-based.
email_note: No public email found after an extensive search. Checked: WebSearch for the business name plus 'email'/'contact', the business name plus phone number (917-306-7075, no hits), the business name plus Facebook/Instagram/Nextdoor/BBB/Thumbtack/HomeAdvisor across Pembroke Pines and nearby Broward/Miami-Dade cities, myfloridalicense.com (DBPR has no individual/handyman license category to search directly), and Sunbiz (Florida Division of Corporations) for 'Alex Handyman' entity names. Multiple similarly-named 'Alex The Handyman' / 'Alex Handyman' businesses exist nationwide (St. Cloud FL, Rancho Cordova CA, East Rockaway NY, North Charleston SC, Calumet Park IL, Kennewick WA, Sugar Hill GA) and regionally (Miami FL Thumbtack profile, Miami HomeAdvisor profile, several Sunbiz LLC filings in Boca Raton and Miami Gardens), none of which could be confirmed as the same entity (no phone number or address match could be verified; Yelp, Thumbtack and HomeAdvisor detail pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches). Per the no-invention rule, none of these speculative leads were used; email left null.
social_note: No verified Instagram or Facebook page found and accepted (see email_note for the same-name businesses found and rejected for lack of a solid phone/address match). Also tried alexthehandyman.com (redirects to a generic '/lander' page, not a real site), alexthehandyman.net (a same-named but clearly unrelated Los Angeles-area business, phone numbers 310-387-9227 and 562-754-8444 found in its markup), thehandymanalex.com (an unrelated Austin, TX WordPress site for 'Next Up Remodeling'), and alexthehandymanllc.com (does not resolve). None belong to this business.
address_note: Google Maps does not publish a street address for this listing (only a pin at 25.782414, -80.2253934 and the city implied by the business name/area). No address field was returned by the live Maps fetch. Per pipeline convention for businesses without a public street address, the site omits the map/address entirely and uses a real work photo in the Contact section instead; JSON-LD address uses city/region only (Pembroke Pines, FL, US).
hours_note: Friday, Saturday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday 7 AM to 9 PM; Sunday open 24 hours. Source: live Google Maps listing fetch, 2026-08-14 (aria-label hours field returned 'Friday, 7 AM to 9 PM'; the brief's full weekly pattern, including the unusual Sunday 24h slot, was cross-confirmed against the task brief's live-verified Maps data from the same day). Used as a differentiator on the site (strip stat and a dedicated contact card) since 24h Sunday availability is a genuinely unusual and real trust signal.
rating_source: Live Google Maps listing fetch (scripts/gmaps_detail.js), confirmed 2026-08-14: rating 5.0. Review count of 14 taken from the task brief's live-verified Maps data captured the same day (the automated Playwright fetch used here returns a signed-out 'limited view' of Maps that does not always expose the numeric review count field, but rating, phone, hours and photos all matched the brief exactly, corroborating the reviewCount figure).
review_themes: Task brief reports recurring review terms: 'honest guy' (3), 'reliability' (3), 'work' (3), 'honest' (4), 'bathroom' (2). No individual verbatim review quotes were available to this research pass (Maps reviews tab did not render review text in the automated fetch), so the site's social-proof section uses the 'razones' (reasons) mode built directly from these verified aggregate themes rather than fabricated quotes, consistent with pipeline rules against inventing testimonial text.
own_site_check: Live Google Maps fetch confirms website: null (the panel shows the 'Add website' prompt Google displays only for listings with no website on file). Tested candidate domains via curl: alexthehandyman.com (200, but redirects via JS to a generic '/lander' page, not a real business site), alexthehandymanpembrokepines.com / alexthehandymanfl.com / alexthehandymanpembroke.com / alexthehandymanllc.com / alexthehandymanflorida.com (all fail to resolve), thehandymanalex.com (200, but a WordPress site for an unrelated Austin, TX company called 'Next Up Remodeling'), alexthehandyman.net (200, but a same-named unrelated Los Angeles-area business with LA-area phone numbers in its markup), alexhandymanservices.com (resolves on http only, empty response body, not usable content). None of these is this business's own website. Conclusion: has_own_site is false.
services_note: No booking platform and no published price list. Services below are derived from two real, verifiable sources: (1) the task brief's live-verified Google review theme tags (honest/honest guy, reliability, work, bathroom), and (2) the business's own uploaded Google Maps photo gallery, scraped live via a custom Playwright script (scripts/gmaps_detail.js extended to open the photo viewer and page through the sidebar thumbnails): 19 unique real photos were found, of which about a dozen clearly depict handyman/carpentry work (bathroom vanity with lit mirror, a modern front door install, a custom walk-in closet build, a wood slat accent wall with mounted TV, a custom loft/bunk bed frame assembly in progress, a bedroom pendant light install, a floating wood shelving unit, a built-in wall unit with electric fireplace, a rolling tool cabinet staged on a job site). A separate cluster of 5 of the 19 photos (from the same uploader, 'alex plishtiev') clearly show the interior of a pet-supply/dog-bakery retail store ('Woof Gang Bakery' signage visible) rather than any handyman work; these were treated as either a past retail build-out job or a stray/mismatched Google Maps photo attribution and were NOT used anywhere on the site (kept out of assets/raw entirely) to avoid presenting a wrong-business image as this handyman's own work. No prices shown anywhere; the site uses 'call for a quote' throughout.

photos.source_note: All photos pulled directly from the business's own Google Maps photo gallery via a custom Playwright scrape (scripts/gmaps_detail.js extended with a photo-viewer 'next' button walk to page through all sidebar thumbnails), run live on 2026-08-14. 19 unique photos found; verified with `file` as valid JPEGs before curation, then visually reviewed one by one (Read tool) before final selection. Downloaded at full resolution (w1600) then resized to max 1000px width, quality ~82, via PIL.

used.desc: Custom built-in wall unit with an integrated electric fireplace and warm lit display shelving either side, finished carpentry and paint. Used as the hero image, og:image and favicon source.

Bathroom vanity with a large backlit LED mirror, tiled countertop, ceiling fan and sconce lighting, finished install. Used as the wide featured gallery tile (ties directly to the 'bathroom' review theme).
Modern dark wood-finish front door installed in an exterior concrete frame. Used in the gallery and reused in the Contact section in place of a map (no public address available).
Custom walk-in closet with built-in pine shelving, hanging rods and a bench, finished install. Used in the gallery.
Custom loft/bunk bed frame mid-assembly, wood slat rails visible, in a bedroom. Used in the gallery as a process shot.
Sculptural black and brass pendant light fixture installed above a bed in a finished bedroom. Used in the gallery.
Floating wood shelving unit under construction against a raw drywall section, tools visible. Used in the gallery as a process shot.
Wood slat accent wall with a wall-mounted TV bracket and a matching floating wood console. Used in the About section.
A rolling tool cabinet, paint supplies and a cordless tool staged on a job site walkway, prepping for a project. Used in the About section.
A built-in wall unit's wood framing and electrical wiring mid-construction, before drywall and finish. Used as the small avatar image (no owner photo/selfie was available in the gallery).

discarded: 5 of the 19 real photos (uploader 'alex plishtiev') show the interior of a pet-supply/dog-bakery retail store with pink shelving and 'Woof Gang Bakery' signage, not handyman work; not used anywhere to avoid presenting the wrong business's interior as this handyman's own work (kept out of assets/raw entirely).
1 photo of an empty room with a sliding glass door and a city view; real but shows no visible work performed, so it was not distinctive enough to include over the 10 stronger photos already selected.
1 dim, low-contrast bedroom photo with a wall-mounted TV, redundant with the wood-slat-wall TV mount photo already used and of lower visual quality; not used.
A near-duplicate second view of the built-in fireplace wall unit was found but not needed given the primary angle already used as the hero image.

palette_note: Indigo/violet palette (accent-deep #694a94, accent-mid #9173bb) on a soft lavender-white base (#e8e1f2), derived by hue-shifting the light-v2 template's token system to hue 265. Chosen to be visually distinct from every other palette built in this repo on 2026-08-14 (blues around hue 208-212, oranges/ambers around hue 24-30, a green around hue 150, and a red-violet around hue -18/342 were all already in use today). The violet reads as premium and trustworthy without repeating any same-day build.
cta_channel: No booking platform, no verified email, no verified social media. Primary CTA is tel:+19173067075 throughout (nav, hero, services cards, CTA final, floating call button); the design system's Instagram/Facebook slot (ig_url, footer social link) is reused to point at the same phone number, labeled 'Phone' instead of 'Instagram', per DESIGN.md/derive.py convention for businesses with no real social presence.
build_note: Built via python3 scripts/derive.py from templates/light-v2/index.html (never edited HTML from scratch) using output/alexthehandymanpembrokepines/content.json as the single source of content. Adapted variant per PIPELINE.md Fase 3.5 for a home-repair/handyman business with no booking platform, no public prices and no public street address: CTA = call/text throughout, services show 'call for a quote', Contact section uses a real work photo (front door install) instead of a map embed, social_proof uses 'razones' mode built from verified aggregate Google review themes instead of fabricated quotes. Bilingual EN default / ES toggle via data-es/data-en + localStorage, matching DESIGN.md Multilenguaje spec. GATE OK: python3 scripts/gate.py alexthehandymanpembrokepines --lang en --forbid "Lash Bloom,Yesi,West Palm,Cresthaven,519855,Pure Artistry,Orlando,pureartistry,_lashbloom". Zero em-dashes, zero <details> elements, all 10 image assets verified to exist and decode, JSON-LD parses valid, no horizontal overflow at 390px viewport (verified with a headless Chromium screenshot).
